title: Third sense: law-rigor ‘mortal’ remains that do not damn those in Christ walking not after the flesh
source_text: XXXII. Tertio peccatum quodvis dicitur mortale quibusdam nostris Theologis, quod habentem, vel peccantem, ex rigore legis morte involveret, si persona absque misericordia Dei in Christo, judicaretur: quamvis jam insito in Christum ad mortem non imputetur, sed remissum sit etiam illi, qui adhuc eodem implicatur. In hisce peccatis ponimus reliquias originalis peccati, quae regeneratis inhaerent, defectus plenariae dilectionis, qui bonis illorum operibus miscuntur, vitiosas denique cupiditates, & motiones quibus repugnant, quasque Sancti gratiae motibus superant, & mortificant, atque in mortali hoc suo corpore dominari non permittunt. Haec omnia, si rei naturam spectes & legem Dei, mortalia sunt; & tamen non damnant eos, iis qui sunt insiti in Christum. Nec simpliciter dixit, Nulla est condemnatio iis qui sunt in Christo Jesu; sed cum additamento hoc, qui non incedunt secundum carnem. Nam quoties renati frena laxantes carni, & concupiscentiis ejus obedientes, incidunt in fornicationem, homicidium, aut consimilia peccata, implicantur reatu mortifero, nec unquam perfrui poterunt vita aeterna, nisi per renovatum actum poenitentiae & fidei ab eodem liberentur.
pass_a_gloss: Thirdly, any sin is called mortal by certain of our theologians which would involve the one having it, or sinning, in death by the rigor of the law, if the person were judged without the mercy of God in Christ: although, now being grafted into Christ, it is not imputed unto death, but is remitted even to him who is still implicated in it. In these sins we place the remains of original sin which inhere in the regenerate, the defects of full love which are mixed with their good works, and finally the vicious desires and motions which they resist, and which the saints overcome and mortify by the motions of grace, and do not permit to reign in this their mortal body. All these, if you look to the nature of the thing and the law of God, are mortal; and yet they do not condemn those who are grafted into Christ. Nor did he say simply, There is no condemnation to them that are in Christ Jesus; but with this addition, who walk not according to the flesh. For as often as the regenerate, loosing the reins to the flesh and obeying its lusts, fall into fornication, homicide, or like sins, they are implicated in death-bringing guilt, nor will they ever be able to enjoy eternal life unless they are freed from it by a renewed act of repentance and faith.
pass_b_english: Third ‘mortal’: law-rigor deserts of remaining corruption that mercy in Christ does not impute unto death.
Romans 8’s ‘no condemnation’ holds for those not walking after the flesh—grave fleshly falls still need renewed repentance.

choices.english: by the rigor of the law
